sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify concerns, supporting reasons and a negotiated proposal. Builds on: essay development and explicit information. Leads to: context clues and directed-writing information.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih: “Rehearsal covers the quiet reading time we agreed.” Ayuk: “The performance is approaching, so we need practice.” Bih: “I understand the deadline. Could we practise spoken parts outside the reading room, then ask the teacher about another time?” Ayuk: “That could protect the quiet period. I will ask whether a suitable space is available.” Bih: “Let us confirm it before changing the notice.” The dialogue reports a proposal, not a confirmed booking.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Locate the relevant sentence, state your answer and identify its support. Check whether a question asks what happened, why, or what cannot be concluded. Do not add a result or private detail that the passage does not provide.
